s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic eruption with skin lesions and liver dysfunction
salient_findings: Pruritic eruption that began on the trunk and spread to all extremities
Scleral icterus and multiple dusky, thin plaques with a central collarette of scale
Hyperkeratotic plaques and deeply seated vesicles with a greenish-black hue on hands and feet
key_facts: Eruption began on the trunk and spread to all extremities
Denied contact allergens, fever, or hyperhidrosis
No prior history of atopic dermatitis, dermatophytosis, or hand eczema
Punch biopsy of the right palm revealed psoriasiform epidermal acanthosis and intraepidermal spongiosis

shortlist.label: Pityriasis rosea
shortlist.why_kept: Punch biopsies of the chest and thigh were consistent with pityriasis rosea

shortlist.label: Porphyria cutanea tarda
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic eruption with skin lesions and liver dysfunction, elevated bilirubin levels

shortlist.label: Primary biliary cirrhosis
shortlist.why_kept: Liver dysfunction with elevated alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin levels

shortlist.label: Primary sclerosing cholangitis
shortlist.why_kept: Liver dysfunction with elevated alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin levels

shortlist.label: Cholestasis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated bilirubin levels and liver dysfunction

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a pruritic eruption with elevated bilirubin levels and liver enzyme abnormalities is most consistent with cholestasis, which is a condition characterized by reduced bile flow and can cause pruritus and skin lesions.

rejected.label: Pityriasis rosea
rejected.why: While punch biopsies of the chest and thigh were consistent with pityriasis rosea, the patient's overall clinical presentation and laboratory findings are more suggestive of a systemic condition like cholestasis.

rejected.label: Porphyria cutanea tarda
rejected.why: The patient's skin lesions and laboratory findings do not specifically suggest porphyria cutanea tarda, which is a disorder of porphyrin metabolism that can cause blistering skin lesions and is often associated with liver disease.

rejected.label: Primary biliary cirrhosis
rejected.why: While the patient has cirrhosis, the presentation and laboratory findings do not specifically suggest primary biliary cirrhosis, which is an autoimmune disease that causes progressive destruction of the bile ducts within the liver.

rejected.label: Primary sclerosing cholangitis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and laboratory findings do not specifically suggest primary sclerosing cholangitis, which is a chronic liver disease characterized by inflammation and scarring of the bile ducts.
